headline: Jonathan Taylor turns trade talk into 'regular scheduled programming' as Colts and Cowboys meet
description: — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins.
story_excerpt: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins. This week, he has heard his named linked to multiple teams, heard about “done deals” and heard some question whether it's wise to even play Sunday when the struggling Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys meet — two days before this season's trade deadline. So Taylor has learned how to laugh it off. All he wants to do is give the fans something to cheer. “It's kind of dragged on for a while now, so at this point, it's just noise,” Taylor said Thursday about the chatter. “It's been like three or four or however many weeks, so at this point, it becomes regular scheduled programming.” It wasn't supposed to be this way after the seven-year veteran who has never played for another team signed a two-year contract extension worth $44 million to stay with the Colts in August. Even then, this week's featured matchup was supposed to be about the brother bash: Indy's veteran receiver Josh Downs and Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs . But with both teams reeling, the older brother requesting a trade and the younger brother in the concussion protocol and dealing with a bad ankle, their dream story may have to wait. That puts the spotlight on Taylor, the franchise's No. 2 career rusher in what could be his final game playing in the Colts — though it's not something he has contemplated. “We've got an opportunity, especially this week — especially after last week — to come back and put a better product on the field,” he said, referring to the embarrassing 42-7 loss to Jacksonville. “That's my biggest goal. Last week was tough. You know you never want to go and put that on display." He just wants to give fans something to cheer about. Indy has (2-6) lost four straight and 13 of 15 and the last time they were home, the boobirds were out in force. Dallas (3-5) hasn't played much better lately. It has the league's worst run defense and has lost three of four after blowing a lead and losing 33-30 in overtime at Arizona last week. So coach Brian Schottenheimer would like nothing better than to ruin Indy's homecoming — even if it Taylor's last stand. “There are certainly a lot of things we as a football team can do better," he said, noting the Cowboys' rushing disparity from Week 7 to Week 8. “I didn’t think we did a great job tackling. headline: Fantasy football: Ranking the best, worst landing spots for Jonathan Taylor
description: It may be just a matter of time before Taylor is dealt, so Michael F. Florio ranks his potential destinations.
story_excerpt: There are two factors that go into determining the best and worst fantasy football landing spots for Jonathan Taylor . The first is what is best for Taylor. I fully believe he is an elite talent and will succeed anywhere. And any team trading for him has to be in a better situation than the Indianapolis Colts , who have traded their top offensive lineman. They have also had poor quarterback play and often trail, which means a negative game script for the running game. However, Taylor is also going to crater the fantasy value of the running backs on whichever team he is dealt to. That should be considered as well. Best Jonathan Taylor landing spots 1. Minnesota Vikings : I would expect any team that acquires Taylor to use him plenty, but the Vikings and their style of play make a lot of sense. They have run the ball at the sixth-highest rate this season. They want to establish the run and trust their defense. Minnesota has created the third-most yards before contact on RB carries, so its offensive line is creating running lanes for the backs. This is a situation where Taylor would get to come in and become the immediate focal point on a team very much in the hunt. It could also help open things up in the passing game, which Justin Jefferson managers would enjoy. Lastly, neither of the Vikings' current running backs is a great fantasy option. Since Jordan Mason returned, neither he nor Aaron Jones Sr . has scored seven fantasy points in a game. 2. Seattle Seahawks : This would ruin the fantasy values of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet , but neither has provided much anyway. The Seahawks have struggled to create consistent running lanes, as evidenced by their 0.6 yards before contact per carry (NFL average: 0.9); however, we should see improvements there with recent acquisition Quenton Nelson on the offensive line. This is the rare instance where Taylor would not be the focal point of opposing defenses, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the perimeter. 3. Cincinnati Bengals : This would hurt in fantasy as it would take Chase Brown out as a weekly option. However, the Bengals' offense would be the NFL version of the "Monstars" with Taylor added. headline: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts
description: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts.
story_excerpt: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court Wednesday, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts, according to federal court records. Rice, who filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, claimed more than $2.1 million of his debts are tied to varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. Rice, 26, has been sued by multiple individuals for his role in a high-speed multicar crash in Dallas in 2024 and an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025. In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in "deferred compensation." The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for "individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors," according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt. The documents claim Rice's largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit. According to the documents, Rice used his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral with Thomas McMurray, his attorney in the pending civil litigations. Rice's bankruptcy attorney, David Shuster, and the Chiefs had no comment about the bankruptcy filing. McMurray did not immediately respond to messages left by ESPN seeking comment. Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract with the Chiefs and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026. He has played in five games this season, with 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Jonathan Taylor 'can't avoid' trade speculation as Colts go through talks
description: Running back Jonathan Taylor, who is the subject of talks between the Colts and multiple teams ahead of the NFL trade deadline, said he's ready for some finality after weeks of speculation about his future.
story_excerpt: INDIANAPOLIS -- As the rest of the NFL awaits the outcome of the Jonathan Taylor trade talks, the Indianapolis Colts star running back says he is just as anxious for a conclusion as everyone else. Taylor, who is the subject of talks between the Colts and multiple teams ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, said he is ready for some finality after weeks of speculation about his future. "No one wants uncertainty," Taylor said Thursday, adding, "Until the past couple weeks, it's kind of been the same thing. But it won't be until Tuesday at [4 p.m.] where you'll know exactly what's going on, you'll know exactly what the verdict is." The Colts (2-6) have been headed for an apparent reboot in recent weeks, beginning with the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last month and the trades of guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner a week later. Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs and others have become trade targets of other teams, as the Colts continue to mull offers with the goal of stockpiling draft picks. As a result, Taylor's future has become one of the biggest stories in the NFL in recent weeks. The Colts' career rushing touchdown leader and second-leading rusher behind Edgerrin James, Taylor, 27, is coveted by teams trying to make a playoff run. "You can't avoid it," Taylor said. "Internet, all of that stuff. You can't avoid it. But it's more about trying to block that out. Let's say you're getting online. Whatever you're getting online to do, go get it done. And whether you have some type of marketing obligation, get it done, and then you're off of it. But you're not going to avoid it, not until it's all over." For now, Taylor is focused on Sunday's home game against the Dallas Cowboys . Indianapolis suffered an embarrassing 42-7 loss at Jacksonville last week, with Taylor held to 23 rushing yards on eight carries. He sat out the fourth quarter because of the huge deficit in the game. Coach Shane Steichen said Taylor will play against the Cowboys despite the trade talks, and Taylor confirmed his intent to play. Sunday's game could be Taylor's last as a member of the Colts, but he said he will focus on winning, not his personal situation. "You don't want external factors creeping in and trying to alter your play," he said.

headline: What 18 contenders should do at the NFL trade deadline: Who could get aggressive?
description: Should the Giants keep adding? Could the Bills go all-in? Would the Steelers stay conservative? Here's how 18 teams at or above .500 should approach the deadline.
story_excerpt: Should your favorite team be going all-in at the NFL trade deadline , which hits at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday? Should it be realistic about its strengths and weaknesses and stay put over the next week? Or is the best plan something in between? Today, I'm going to answer those questions for the 18 teams that reached Week 9 at .500 or better. Given their roster and play this season, I believe that four teams should stand down at the deadline and avoid sacrificing serious draft capital for any moves. Nobody is going to turn down a steal of a deal if one is available, but those four franchises shouldn't be prioritizing major additions. Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' But as for the rest, I've split the other 14 teams into several tiers, ranging from organizations that should be extremely active at the deadline to ones that should be very selective and careful about making the right move for a very particular sort of player. I'll lay out each team's needs and current situation. I'll also name two possible trade candidates for each team. One will be a luxury trade addition, where the team would be adding a starter or even a borderline star to the roster and paying accordingly for the privilege. The other is a bargain deal, where the team would instead be looking for a rotational player or depth for the back of its roster. (Teams are listed alphabetically within each tier.) Buffalo Bills (6-1) Positions of need: OL, LB, S Was Buffalo's 36-10 victory over the Ravens a sign that defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was able to find the right mix of players and pressures during the bye week or a product of the Ravens being stuck playing Joe Fagnano at quarterback for most of the game? I'd lean more toward the latter than the former, but I also wouldn't be shocked if Leonhard's defense took a step forward after having a week to rest and reflect on what went wrong early in the season. headline: Could the Panthers make a trade deadline move? 5 potential targets
description: Let's dive into which players could make sense for a trade for the NFC South-leading team with limited cap space.
story_excerpt: The Carolina Panthers remain an intriguing team just a few days before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. Even at 3-4, the Panthers will be in the mix for a second consecutive NFC South division title, regardless of the results of Week 9's home game against the Denver Broncos (6-2) on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ). That's life in the NFC South, where no team is above .500, and the Panthers, despite their up-and-down start to the season, remain at the top entering the midway point of the campaign. A plausible case can be made for the Panthers to add reinforcements at the deadline. There's also a reasonable case to trade away an expensive and/or underperforming player, especially if a contender offers a quality draft pick in return. General manager Dan Morgan could also, as he did last year, simply stay put with his roster and hope history repeats itself with the Panthers on top of a forgettable divisional scrum in January. The Panthers have limited salary cap space ($684,323, as of Wednesday, according to the NFLPA salary cap report). But they have the flexibility -- like all NFL teams -- to maneuver their cap situation with contract restructures that would open up space while pushing current cap charges into the future. Still, it's more likely the Panthers look for a bargain (particularly players on rookie deals) than a big name on the trade market. Here's a look at three players who could make sense to add before the deadline and two internal players who might garner trade interest with an advantageous exit: Three players the Panthers could add: Jackson Powers-Johnson , G/C, Las Vegas Raiders Age: 23 | Stats: Seven games (four starts) in 2026; 30 games (25 starts) in three seasons. Why Powers-Johnson makes sense for Panthers: Powers-Johnson, a 2024 second-round pick, probably needs a change of scenery after being benched in Las Vegas. He has guard/center versatility, and while the Panthers just activated Brady Christensen's 21-day practice window on injured reserve, Powers-Johnson is cost-effectively signed through 2027 ($1.6 million base salary in 2026 and just under $2 million next year). The former Oregon standout doesn't have to start immediately to be valuable, but he'd be a clear upgrade as the swing interior backup if Christensen or Sam Hecht gets the call to replace center Luke Fortner .
